identification.summary: Microsoft describes Storm-0978 (also DEV-0978; called RomCom by other vendors, after its backdoor) as a Russia-based cybercriminal group that runs opportunistic ransomware and extortion-only operations plus targeted credential-gathering campaigns that likely support intelligence operations [S1]. Microsoft links it to prior management of the Industrial Spy ransomware market and crypter [S1]. Cisco Talos tracks related activity as UAT-5647, a Russian-speaking cluster also known as RomCom [S2]. ESET calls the group Russia-aligned and assessed a 2025 operation as espionage [S4].
identification.firstObserved: RomCom backdoor activity against Ukrainian military targets and spoofed-software sites was reported by BlackBerry in late 2022 [S5]. Microsoft dates Industrial Spy ransomware to May 2022 and fake-installer phishing to October 2022 [S1]. Talos reports UAT-5647 activity since at least late 2023 [S2].
identification.notes: Aliases stated by sources: DEV-0978, RomCom [S1]; UAT-5647 [S2]; Void Rabisu, Tropical Scorpius, UNC2596 [S5][S6]; Underground Team (ransom-note name for the Underground ransomware) [S1]. Cluster boundaries differ by vendor: Microsoft's description centres on ransomware plus credential theft, Talos on a Ukraine/Poland espionage cluster, Trend Micro on a possibly Cuba-linked criminal group [S1][S2][S6]. Treat vendor aliases as overlapping, not identical, until vendors publish mapping evidence.

attribution.sponsor: No government sponsor is named in the sources gathered. Microsoft characterises Storm-0978 as a Russia-based cybercriminal group [S1]. ESET describes RomCom as Russia-aligned [S3][S4]. Reporting on Trend Micro's assessment says there is no evidence of state sponsorship and that the group may be a financially motivated criminal group drawn into espionage by the war in Ukraine [S6].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft's assessment is that the group is cybercriminal with espionage-supporting credential campaigns [S1]. Talos describes UAT-5647 as Russian-speaking [S2]. ESET assesses espionage motive for the 2025 WinRAR operation [S4]. No vendor in these sources attributes the group to a named Russian state organization.
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and malware analysis, including Industrial Spy and Underground ransomware code overlap and the CERT-UA-reported compromise of a Ukrainian MoD email account [S1]; Talos analysis of malware variants and keyboard-language checks [S2]; ESET zero-day discovery [S3][S4]; BlackBerry and Trend Micro infrastructure and tooling reporting [S5][S6].

objectives: Mixed financial and intelligence objectives: opportunistic ransomware and extortion, plus credential gathering likely supporting intelligence operations against Ukrainian government and military targets and entities with Ukraine ties [S1]. Talos assesses a staged strategy of long-term access and data exfiltration for espionage, then potential pivot to ransomware [S2]. ESET assessed espionage as the motive for the July 2025 WinRAR operation [S4].

regions: Poland (assessed by Talos from malware keyboard-language checks) [S2]
targeting.notes: Microsoft: espionage-style targeting hit government and military organizations mainly in Ukraine and defense/government entities in Europe and North America with possible Ukraine ties; ransomware victims were largely opportunistic and included telecommunications and finance [S1]. ESET observed Firefox/Windows exploit victims mostly in Europe and North America [S3]. ESET reported no successful compromises from the July 2025 WinRAR phishing, per search coverage of its research [S4].

capabilities.summary: Initial access: trojanized or look-alike installer sites for software such as Adobe products, Advanced IP Scanner, SolarWinds, KeePass and Signal [S1][S5]; phishing with lure documents including a compromised Ukrainian MoD email account (CERT-UA, December 2022) [S1]; spear-phishing with downloaders [S2]. Zero-day use: CVE-2023-36884 Microsoft Office/Word RCE in June 2023 with NATO and Ukrainian World Congress lures [S1]; chained Firefox CVE-2024-9680 and Windows Task Scheduler CVE-2024-49039 in 2024, reported by ESET as RomCom's second in-the-wild zero-day [S3]; WinRAR path-traversal CVE-2025-8088 in July 2025 [S4]. Malware: RomCom backdoor/RAT [S1], SingleCamper RAT variant, RustyClaw and MeltingClaw downloaders, DustyHammock and ShadyHammock backdoors [S2]; SnipBot variant, RustyClaw and a Mythic agent in the 2025 WinRAR chain (per search coverage) [S4]. Post-exploitation: Impacket SMBExec/WMIExec for lateral movement and SAM hive dumping for credentials [S1]. Ransomware: Industrial Spy, Underground (assessed by Microsoft as possibly an Industrial Spy rebrand) and Trigona in at least one attack [S1]. Microsoft says the actor reportedly acquired zero-day exploits [S1].

campaigns.name: Industrial Spy ransomware and marketplace
campaigns.summary: Microsoft dates first sightings of Industrial Spy ransomware to May 2022 and links Storm-0978 to management of its market and crypter. A US advisory reports third-party reporting that Cuba ransomware actors began selling stolen data on the Industrial Spy marketplace around May 2022.

campaigns.name: Fake installer sites and spoofed software
campaigns.summary: Look-alike sites for SolarWinds NPM, KeePass, PDF Reader Pro and others delivered the RomCom RAT; BlackBerry linked related artifacts to attacks on Ukrainian military institutions and noted some English-speaking countries including the UK were targeted.

campaigns.name: Compromised Ukrainian MoD email account
campaigns.summary: Per CERT-UA as cited by Microsoft, a Ukrainian Ministry of Defense email account was compromised and used to send phishing; information-stealing malware was hosted on an actor-controlled site.

campaigns.name: CVE-2023-36884 Office zero-day phishing
campaigns.summary: Phishing with NATO and Ukrainian World Congress lures against defense and government entities in Europe and North America exploited an Office RCE before disclosure; Microsoft patched on 2023-08-08. Ransomware ran concurrently against an unrelated target.

campaigns.name: Underground ransomware
campaigns.summary: Microsoft observed Underground ransomware (ransom notes signed Underground team) with code similarity to Industrial Spy, and assesses it may be a rebrand.

campaigns.name: Targeting of female political leaders (Void Rabisu)
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro reported a new RomCom variant used against women political leaders; coverage notes Trend's view that the group is possibly financially motivated and drawn into espionage by the war in Ukraine. Details come from secondary coverage; the Trend Micro report was not opened.

campaigns.name: UAT-5647 campaigns against Ukraine and Poland
campaigns.summary: Talos reported activity since at least late 2023 against Ukrainian government entities and unidentified Polish entities using SingleCamper, RustyClaw, MeltingClaw, DustyHammock and ShadyHammock, and assessed a staged espionage-then-possible-ransomware strategy.

campaigns.name: Firefox and Windows zero-day chain
campaigns.summary: ESET found CVE-2024-9680 (Firefox, found 2024-10-08, patched next day) chained with CVE-2024-49039 (Windows Task Scheduler, patched 2024-11-12; also found independently by Google TAG) for code execution after visiting a malicious page; victims mostly in Europe and North America; RomCom backdoor delivered.

campaigns.name: WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 spear-phishing
campaigns.summary: Per coverage of ESET research, job-application-themed spear-phishing from 2025-07-18 to 2025-07-21 used a WinRAR zero-day to deliver SnipBot variant, RustyClaw and Mythic agent against companies in Europe and Canada; ESET reported no successful compromises. WinRAR 7.13 fixed the flaw on 2025-07-30.

diamond.adversary: Russia-based or Russia-aligned group with mixed criminal and espionage activity; no state sponsor named in sources [S1][S3][S6].
diamond.capability: RomCom family backdoors and downloaders, zero-day exploits (CVE-2023-36884, CVE-2024-9680/49039, CVE-2025-8088), Impacket, and Industrial Spy/Underground ransomware [S1][S2][S3][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Look-alike software download domains (for example advanced-ip-scaner[.]com), actor-controlled sites hosting stealers, a Tor leak site for Underground, and a compromised Ukrainian MoD mailbox for phishing [S1][S5].
diamond.victim: Ukrainian government and military, defense and government bodies in Europe and North America with Ukraine ties, Polish entities, political leaders, and opportunistic ransomware victims in telecommunications and finance [S1][S2][S6].
diamond.socioPolitical: Russia's war in Ukraine and NATO support for it drive the espionage lures and targets; Trend Micro suggests the war pulled a criminal group toward espionage [S1][S6].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints, Office, WinRAR, Firefox/Thunderbird/Tor Browser, and users who download admin tools from search results [S1][S3][S4].

gaps: No source gathered ties the group to a named Russian state organization; sponsor attribution is open.

Cluster mapping is unsettled: Microsoft Storm-0978, Talos UAT-5647, Trend Micro Void Rabisu, Unit 42 Tropical Scorpius and UNC2596 overlap, but the vendor evidence for equating them, and the claimed Cuba ransomware link, was not verified here (Trend Micro treats the Cuba link as inference per secondary coverage) [S5][S6].

Primary documents not opened: Cisco Talos, ESET WeLiveSecurity, BlackBerry, Trend Micro and Unit 42 blogs failed to load or were unavailable; those findings rely on search-result summaries and secondary coverage.
No reporting after August 2025 was found in this research; current activity is unknown.
The ESET WinRAR report also names other actors exploiting the same flaw; that detail was not verified.
MITRE ATT&CK group ID not present in the record; ATT&CK mapping not attempted.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the user endpoint and the software supply path: admin-tool download sites, mail gateways, archive utilities, browsers and Office, plus allied government mailboxes that can be abused as trusted senders [S1][S3][S4]. STEP 2: The actor reuses public lures (NATO, Ukraine, job applications) and has repeatedly fielded zero-days, so defenders face short patch windows [S1][S3][S4]. STEP 3: Template is lure or fake installer, then RomCom-family backdoor, then Impacket lateral movement and credential theft, with ransomware possible [S1][S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued spear-phishing and trojanized-software campaigns against Ukraine-supporting government, defense and telecom entities in Europe and North America. MDCOA is a fresh zero-day used against coalition personnel with a ransomware pivot that disrupts mission systems [S1][S2]. Candidate indicators: look-alike domains for admin tools, Office or archive tools spawning child processes, SAM hive export, Impacket SMBExec/WMIExec activity, and WinRAR versions at or below 7.12 [S1][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track vendor zero-day disclosures for Office, browsers and archive tools and push patch status to operators quickly [S1][S3][S4]. (2) Authorities: coordinate any response beyond owned networks through the appropriate cyber authorities; the sources give no state sponsor to justify escalation. (3) Mission assurance: ransomware pivot risk argues for offline backups and segmentation of mission networks [S1][S2]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with allied and DIB partners, since targeting spans Europe, Canada and North America [S3][S4].
